$comment: Recreates the five pages of the Figma reference (examples/figma-sms-credit-guide) for visual comparison.

pages.title: How Salesmsg
pages.subtitle: Understand segments, character limits, and what comes off your balance.

blocks.heading: The basics
blocks.intro: Texting is billed in segments. Most short, plain-text messages fit in one segment. Longer messages and messages using Unicode can need more segments. Calling, voicemail, and AI features have their own rates.

rows.definition: Every letter, number, space, and symbol counts.
The standard character set for plain text and common punctuation.
The expanded character set used for emojis and non-Latin scripts.
A segment is one billed text unit. One SMS segment costs one credit.

blocks.heading: How a text turns into credits
blocks.footnote: Long messages use some space for a header that lets the recipient’s phone reassemble the segments into one continuous message.

pages.title: What each
pages.subtitle: A quick reference for messaging, calling, voicemail, and AI features.

rows.label: SMS
rows.note: Inbound and outbound. See the character limits on page 1.

rows.label: MMS
rows.note: Picture or media message. Flat rate, regardless of length.

rows.label: RCS
rows.note: Same as MMS, including international. Failed attempts are charged.

rows.label: Ringless voicemail
rows.note: Flat rate for each voicemail delivered.

rows.label: Calling
rows.note: Standard U.S. number: 1 credit per minute. Other rates vary.

rows.label: Call forwarding
rows.note: Starts when the forwarded call rings, even if unanswered.

rows.label: Transcription
rows.note: For calls and voicemails, including the AI summary.

rows.label: AI agent messages
rows.note: Added to SMS, MMS, or RCS for each message the agent reads or writes.

rows.label: AI calling agent
rows.note: Depends on your plan. Ask your Customer Success Manager.

rows.label: Enterprise / custom
rows.note: Negotiated activity rates, including the premium Salesforce integration.

blocks.title: Credits and carrier fees are separate
blocks.text: U.S. and Canadian carrier surcharges and 10DLC one-time and monthly fees appear separately on your invoice. They are passed through at cost and do not reduce your credit balance.

pages.title: Calling rates & your
pages.subtitle: Know which rates vary, which credits carry forward, and what happens at zero.

blocks.heading: Calling and international rates
blocks.intro: For inbound calls, the rate depends on your own inbox number. For outbound calls and texts, it depends on the contact’s country.

paragraphs.text: by country and route, for inbound and outbound texting and calling. Salesmsg supports 236 countries; see the Help Center for the full credit list.
If disabled, only U.S., Canadian, U.K., and Australian numbers are valid. Other destinations are rejected.

rows.definition: Monthly credits reset on your billing anniversary. Annual credits are granted in full on your renewal date. Unused plan credits do not carry forward.
One-off purchases and auto-recharge top-ups remain until you use them.
Messages and calls cannot go out until you top up. Inbound texts still arrive and can take the balance negative; the shortfall comes off your next purchase.
If credits are insufficient for a broadcast or voicemail drop, Salesmsg prompts you to buy more before sending.

blocks.title: Keep your account running
blocks.text: Set an auto-recharge threshold and top-up amount, and add a backup card. Call forwarding requires auto-recharge to be enabled.

pages.title: Make every
pages.subtitle: Worked examples, simple sending habits, and answers to common questions.

paragraphs.text: Aim comfortably below 160 characters. Link to detail instead of sending several segments. Use simple punctuation and paste as plain text. Use emojis deliberately: they can switch the message to Unicode and lower the single-segment limit to 70. Check the composer’s segment counter before sending.

rows.label: RCS fails, then falls back to SMS / MMS

blocks.title: See where your credits went
blocks.text: The in-app credit usage report breaks down messages, calls, AI agent, transcripts, and Salesforce, with logs and exports. Your Customer Success Manager can walk through it with you.

pages.title: Check before
pages.subtitle: A single Unicode character can change the cost of the whole message.

blocks.title: The whole message uses the same encoding
blocks.text: An emoji or a character outside GSM-7 switches the entire message to Unicode. Curly quotes and em dashes pasted from other apps can do this too.

blocks.heading: Same length. Different credit use
blocks.footnote: A short pickup message can still fit in one segment with or without an emoji. The difference matters when the message exceeds its encoding’s single-segment limit.

items.question: Why did a short message cost 2 credits?
items.answer: Check for a Unicode character. One can lower the whole message’s single-segment limit to 70 characters.

items.question: Do customer replies cost credits?
items.answer: Yes. Inbound messages use the same rates as outbound, even when your balance is zero.

items.question: Do unused credits carry forward?
items.answer: Purchased credits do. Plan credits reset each billing period.

items.question: Where can I see my usage?
items.answer: Open the credit usage report for activity breakdowns, logs, and exports. Your Customer Success Manager can help.
